source: Ichien, Lin, Holyoak & Lu (2024) Cognitive complexity explains processing asymmetry in judgments of similarity versus difference (Exp 1)
finding: Human relational difference is harder to detect than relational similarity. Featural trials show no gap. The authors argue this complexity account explains the similarity/difference asymmetry better than alignability.
numbers: N=184 UCLA students (98 similarity, 86 difference). Unambiguous relational trials: similarity M=.81, difference M=.69, z=4.81, p<.001. Featural trials: .84 vs .84, p=.966. Verbal task similarity .80, visual .86. Gap survived controlling for Raven score.
limits: Online undergraduates; word pairs and geometric shapes only. Not about LLMs. It re-explains, rather than refutes, the alignability result for similarity-vs-difference judgments.
agent_relevance: Asking an agent what differs loads relational structure harder than asking what is shared. Expect worse relational difference detection and consider asking for both views (G, S2).

source: Ichien et al. (2024) Cognitive complexity ... (Exp 2, stories)
finding: With Gentner et al. (1993) Karla-the-hawk stories, relational responding depended on whether people processed each story separately before comparing. The asymmetry shrank when stories were shown one at a time.
numbers: N=129. Presentation x comparison-type interaction chi2(1)=4.82, p=.03. Mean trial time incremental 52.3 s (similarity) and 59.9 s (difference) vs simultaneous 45.0 s and 43.1 s.
limits: Between-subject; interaction only just significant (p=.03). Stories are the classic Gentner stimulus set, but this team is not the Gentner lab.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: heavy stimuli (stories) get shallow comparison if shown side by side without prior encoding. Suggests encoding each case first, then comparing (S2).

source: Estes & Hasson (2004) The importance of being nonalignable (as reported in Ichien et al. 2024 and a search abstract)
finding: Independent critical test of Markman and Gentner: nonalignable differences exerted a larger effect than alignable ones in similarity and difference judgments of geometric stimuli.
numbers: Only the direction is stated in the sources seen (nonalignable > alignable). No effect sizes extracted.
quote: nonalignable differences exerted a greater impact than alignable differences
limits: Not opened. Cited second-hand through Ichien et al. (opened) and a search snippet. Geometric stimuli, not words or stories.
agent_relevance: First independent contradiction of K02 in our files. The alignable-over-nonalignable weighting is not universal, so K02 should not be treated as an agent design rule.

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Reply to Hodel and West and to Lewis and Mitchell. Shuffled-alphabet letter strings fail mostly because the model must count letter positions. GPT-4 with code execution reached human level.
numbers: Human N=99 (interval 1) and N=97 (interval 2). Interval-size effect: humans P=1.5e-11, GPT-4 P<2e-16, GPT-4+code P=0.066. Humans vs GPT-4 P=8.9e-13; humans vs GPT-4+code P=0.496. 46% of GPT-4 errors were a valid alternative rule vs 39% in human errors reported by Lewis and Mitchell.
limits: Authors are the original authors. Code execution is a non-human route. GPT-4 only. Single task variant tested here.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly closed: the disputed failure is a tool-use and counting failure, so an agent should be given code for index lookup rather than blamed for weak analogy.

source: Hodel & West (2023) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Rerun of Webb et al. letter-string tasks with a synthetic alphabet and larger interval. GPT-3 collapsed while humans stayed steady. Comprehension checks show GPT-3 understood the permuted alphabet at least partly.
numbers: GPT-3 generative accuracy under 0.1 on extend-sequence, successor, predecessor and fix-alphabetic-sequence with synthetic alphabet. Only remove-redundant-letter and sort stayed near original levels. Comprehension checks: at least 30% of original level on all but predecessor.
limits: GPT-3 only (text-davinci-003). Pre-dates the code-execution counter-argument.
agent_relevance: Side A of gap 8. With d04 it shows the dispute turns on counting and tool access.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs (protocol details)
finding: Protocol read in full: 136 Prolific participants, 14 problems each, permuted alphabets n=0,2,5,10,20 plus a symbol alphabet; counterfactual comprehension checks run on GPT models.
numbers: Samples per permutation level for models: n=0: 276, n=2: 336, n=5: 270, n=10: 342, n=20: 384, symbol: 268. Headline accuracies (humans .753; GPT-3 .488; GPT-3.5 .350; GPT-4 .452) were already confirmed in critique.md.
limits: No code-execution arm and no error-type scoring in the protocol. This is the open design hole behind gap 8.
agent_relevance: A fixed protocol for the dispute needs: code on/off, interval size 1 vs 2, and valid-alternative-rule scoring. It cannot be run here (no model access this session).

source: Musker, Duchnowski, Milliere & Pavlick (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning (J. Memory and Language 145)
finding: New tasks map semantically rich words to symbol patterns. Advanced LLMs match humans in several conditions but differ on task variations and semantic distractors. Humans keep the mapping when pair order is permuted; LLM performance drops.
numbers: Humans: 132 (semantic structure study) and 62 (semantic content study) Brown students. Claude 3 is significantly worse than humans in some conditions (coef -1.05, z=-2.80, p=.005).
limits: Two-column PDF text was partly scrambled; only the abstract-level result and a few regression lines were read cleanly. 2024-era models.
agent_relevance: Mapping under re-representation is where models still diverge. S2 should hold alignment pairs fixed and test order-robustness (G).

source: Choi et al. (2024) AnaloBench: Benchmarking the identification of abstract and long-context analogies (EMNLP 2024, T1 selection)
finding: When four candidates are given, models pick the analogous story well for one-sentence stories but fall as stories get long. Scale helps little for long stories. Human accuracy stays high.
limits: Long versions were written by GPT-4; a check with Claude-written stories left GPT-4 near unchanged (60.7 on GPT-4 generations vs 57.6 on Claude generations at 30 sentences, as read from the table). Humans were run on few instances.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: with candidates already in context, mapping works at short length. Degradation with length points to attention and noise, not a lack of mapping.

source: Choi et al. (2024) AnaloBench (T2 retrieval from a story bank)
finding: Finding analogous stories from a large bank is near random for the best models, even though they can choose among four options when candidates are supplied. Retrieval, not mapping, is the main bottleneck.
numbers: GPT-4-Turbo beat the random-k baseline only in the single-sentence bank; in 10- and 30-sentence banks both tested models were near the trivial baseline (30-sentence bank about 110K tokens).
limits: Precision-recall curves in the paper; exact figures per k are in Appendix Table 8, not extracted here. Only two proprietary models in T2.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 answer: far-analogy failure is largely retrieval. For the agent, store cases with relational summaries and retrieve by structure, then compare in context (S2).

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners, Table 4 (retrieved vs self-generated vs fixed)
finding: On GSM8K, self-generated exemplars beat retrieved ones for the strongest base model but not for weaker ones. Authors say retrieval does better for smaller models.
numbers: text-davinci-003: 5-shot fixed CoT 50%, retrieved 54%, self-generated 61%; text-davinci-002: 43/47/48; weaker davinci/curie models: 2-11%, retrieved at least as good. GPT-3.5-turbo GSM8K: 0-shot 75.0, 0-shot CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated 77.8; MATH 33.0/33.9/34.9/37.3. Codeforces Acc@1 GPT-3.5-16k: 3-shot 11%, self-gen 13%, self-gen knowledge+exemplars 15%; GPT-4 17% to 19%.
limits: Table cells are partly misaligned in the pdf text; row identity for davinci-003 and 002 inferred from the caption. 2023 models. Mild gains (+1.1 GSM8K for GPT-3.5 over 5-shot).
agent_relevance: Gap 4 answer: self-generation helps mostly when the model is strong enough to produce good analogues, and mostly on diverse or algorithmic tasks (MATH, Codeforces), not easy arithmetic.

source: Kim et al. (2022) Self-generated in-context learning (SG-ICL)
finding: Letting the model write its own demonstrations beats zero-shot and has lower variance than randomly picked gold demonstrations.
numbers: Worth about 0.6 gold training samples on four text classification tasks.
limits: Small tasks and older models; classification, not reasoning. Worth about 0.6 gold samples means the gain is modest.
agent_relevance: Earlier evidence that self-made examples are a weak substitute for real ones. Supports using retrieved real cases when available.

source: Yu et al. (2024) Thought Propagation: an analogical approach to complex reasoning with LLMs (ICLR 2024)
finding: The model solves analogous problems first and reuses their solutions or plans for the new input. Gains are largest on weaker backends and tasks needing planning.
numbers: Shortest-path, 0-shot optimal rate: GPT-3.5 TP 0.65 vs CoT 0.26 vs IO 0.33; PaLM-2 0.36 vs 0.24; GPT-4 IO 0.78, CoT 0.76. Creative writing coherence GPT-3.5 7.000 vs CoT 6.654; GPT-4 7.989 vs 7.684; user preference 39%/45% vs CoT 21%/15%.
limits: Compute is higher (several calls); no alignable-difference measurement; GPT-4 shortest-path is already near ceiling.
agent_relevance: Related to S2 reuse of solved neighbours. Gain on strong models is small, matching Yasunaga's pattern.

source: Chia et al. (2023) Contrastive chain-of-thought prompting, Table 1 ablation
finding: Preliminary ablation of invalid-rationale types. All kinds of invalid contrast beat plain CoT, so the effect is not specific to one corruption type.
numbers: GPT-3.5: standard 27.4/11.2 (GSM8K/Bamboogle), CoT 69.2/40.8, +invalid reasoning 76.0/45.6, +incoherent objects 79.6/53.6, +incoherent language 78.8/52.8, +irrelevant objects 79.8/48.8, +irrelevant language 80.2/49.6. AQuA gain alone +4.0, with self-consistency an extra +14.2.
limits: One model family (GPT-3.5); 500-sample test caps; no reasoning model; invalid rationales built by shuffling spans, not by aligned counterexamples.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partial: valid-plus-invalid contrast helps non-reasoning models. Whether it matches human comparison gains is untested since corruptions are not alignable differences.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: incentivizing reasoning capability in LLMs via RL
finding: The authors report that few-shot prompting consistently degrades R1 and recommend zero-shot prompts that describe the problem and output format.
numbers: No numbers in the passage: qualitative statement in the prompt-engineering note.
quote: Few-shot prompting consistently degrades its performance.
limits: Single developer report; no table of few-shot vs zero-shot. One reasoning model family; unclear for contrastive demonstrations specifically.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: demonstration-based S2 (valid plus invalid examples) may hurt reasoning models. Prefer instruction-level comparison steps, and test before relying on it.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs self-compose reasoning structures
finding: Forcing the model to select, adapt and implement an explicit reasoning structure beats free-form CoT at far lower cost than ensembling. This is structure forcing, not correspondence listing.
numbers: PaLM 2-L BBH/T4D/MATH: direct 56/30/45, CoT 60/40/42, Self-Discover 67/69/50.5. GPT-4: direct 58/51/70.5, CoT 75/52/71, Self-Discover 81/85/73. Uses 10-40x fewer inference calls than self-consistency-style methods.
limits: Not a comparison task; gain at equal tokens versus a matched free-form control is not tested; GPT-4 and PaLM 2 of 2023.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: nearest evidence that explicit structure beats free form for LLMs, but it does not answer the S2 question (correspondence listing at equal tokens).

source: Alfieri, Nokes-Malach & Schunn (2013) Learning through case comparisons: a meta-analytic review
finding: Could not be opened: the lab URL returns an HTML page (HTTP 404 on fetch) and ERIC reset the connection; the Semantic Scholar record exists but rate limits blocked the abstract.

source: Search status (2026-11-10) for independent replications of analogical encoding and for follow-ups to ARN and StoryAnalogy
finding: WebSearch budget was spent by parallel agents; arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned 429 for most calls. An independent (non-Gentner-lab) replication of analogical encoding was not found.
numbers: Zero new independent replication effect sizes obtained this run.
